name: i18n

hero.title: `count === 1` is not a plural rule.
hero.lede: Translations, plurals, prices and dates that follow each language's own rules, and switch language live without a reload or a re-render. The message format is i18next's, so your JSON files come with you.

facts.value: {dot:ok} `t()`, plurals, locale switch<small>Lowered to a native runtime, asserted on device. Native targets are experimental; live switching and full CLDR plurals come in the next release.</small>

why.title: The bugs you ship in your second language, gone.

items.title: Plurals by the language, not by `=== 1`
items.text: Czech says 1 soubor, 3 soubory, 5 souborů. Polish says 22 pliki and 25 plików. `t('files', { count })` asks `Intl.PluralRules` for the category and picks `files_few` or `files_many` for you.

items.title: Switch language, nothing re-renders
items.text: `i18n.locale.set('pl')` and every `t()`, price and date on screen rewrites its own text node. Components keep their state, inputs keep their caret.

items.title: Formats live inside the message
items.text: Write `Total: {{amount, currency}}` or `Seen {{n, relativetime, day}}` in the translation. Translators move the number; you never concatenate.

items.title: Same messages on the server
items.text: `@pyreon/i18n/core` has no JSX and depends only on `@pyreon/reactivity`, so receipts, emails and edge functions use the same dictionaries as the UI.

difference.title: You have written this ternary. So has everyone.

before.label: the usual shortcut
before.caption: Right in English and German. Wrong in Czech, Polish, Russian, Ukrainian and Arabic.

after.label: with @pyreon/i18n
after.caption: Each language lists the forms it has. The count picks one. A missing locale falls back.
after.code:
import { createI18n } from '@pyreon/i18n'

const i18n = createI18n({
  locale: 'cs',
  fallbackLocale: 'en',
  messages: {
    en: { files_one: '{{count}} file', files_other: '{{count}} files' },
    cs: { files_one: '{{count}} soubor', files_few: '{{count}} soubory',
          files_other: '{{count}} souborů' },
    pl: { files_one: '{{count}} plik', files_few: '{{count}} pliki',
          files_many: '{{count}} plików', files_other: '{{count}} pliku' },
  },
})

i18n.t('files', { count: 3 })   // '3 soubory'
i18n.t('files', { count: 5 })   // '5 souborů'
i18n.locale.set('pl')           // every t() on screen updates in place
i18n.t('files', { count: 22 })  // '22 pliki'

comingFrom.title: Keep the JSON. Drop the init.
comingFrom.after:
import { createI18n } from '@pyreon/i18n'

const i18n = createI18n({
  locale: 'cs',
  fallbackLocale: 'en',
  messages: { en, cs },   // the same objects
})

i18n.t('files', { count: 3 })  // '3 soubory'
i18n.locale.set('en')          // synchronous, and reactive
comingFrom.note: Checked with the same `en`/`cs` objects in both libraries: interpolation, `_one`/`_few`/`_other`, `context`, nested keys, `$t()` nesting and fallback give the same strings. Not supported: ordinal plurals, the `{{- raw}}` prefix and inline format options such as `number(minimumFractionDigits: 2)` (use a named format). i18next HTML-escapes values by default; Pyreon writes text into text nodes, so it does not.

comingFrom.title: ICU plurals become suffix keys.
comingFrom.note: Pyreon does not parse ICU MessageFormat: each plural branch becomes its own `_one`/`_other` key, and `{name}` becomes `{{name}}`. Numbers, dates, relative time and lists go through the same `Intl` formatters as `formatNumber` and friends, as `i18n.n()`, `d()` and `rt()`, with `l()` for lists in the next release.

demo.title: Change the language, then the count.
demo.text: Pick Czech or Polish and try 1, 2, 5, 22 and 1.5. The plural category comes from `Intl.PluralRules`, the same call the package makes, and the price, date and relative time re-format for the new locale.
demo.referenceHtml:
Try 0, 1, 2, 5, 22 and 1.5
plural category:
n(1234.5, currency)
d(now, date)
rt(-3, day)
n(0.42, percent)

features.title: The whole translation layer, in one instance.

items.name: `t(key, values)`
items.text: Reactive: read it in JSX and the text node updates when the locale or the messages change.

items.name: CLDR plurals
items.text: `_zero` through `_many` per language, plus an explicit `_zero` for "No files" and your own `pluralRules`.

items.name: `n()`, `d()`, `rt()`
items.text: Numbers, currency, dates and relative time, with each `Intl` formatter cached per locale and options.

items.name: Inline format specs
items.text: `{{when, date}}`, `{{n, relativetime, day}}` and your own named formats, such as `{{amount, currency}}`, inside the message.

items.name: `l()` and `dir()`
items.text: Lists in code or as `{{people, list}}`, and `rtl` for Arabic or Hebrew, ready for `<html dir>`.

items.name: Context and defaults
items.text: `{ context: 'female' }` tries `friend_female` first; `defaultValue` covers a key nobody translated yet.

items.name: Namespaces on demand
items.text: `t('checkout:title')` with a `loader`; two concurrent loads of one namespace make one request.

items.name: `<Trans>`
items.text: Puts JSX inside a translation: `<bold>rich</bold>` maps to your component, with `t` read from the provider.

items.name: Typed keys, opt in
items.text: `createI18n<typeof en>()` turns `t('nav.hoem')` into a compile error.

items.name: Devtools subpath
items.text: `@pyreon/i18n/devtools` lists live instances and their loaded locales, held by `WeakRef`.

recipes.title: Load a namespace when the route needs it
recipes.text: Ship only the strings the page uses. Concurrent loads of the same namespace share one request, and `t()` updates when it lands.

recipes.title: Translate a receipt email on the server
recipes.text: The `/core` entry has no JSX. The same dictionaries render in a worker, with currency and date formatted for the reader.

api.title: Eight runtime exports and one instance.

limits.title: Give each language its own plural keys
limits.text: The category is chosen per locale. A Czech dictionary with only `_one` and `_other` falls back to `_other` for 3, which reads wrong. Add `_few` and `_many` where the language has them.

limits.title: Pluralize with `count`
limits.text: `count` drives the plural choice; a number passed as `n` or `value` is interpolated but not pluralized. `context` and `defaultValue` are options too, not message variables.

limits.title: Read formatters in reactive code
limits.text: `n()`, `d()` and `rt()` read the locale signal. Call them in JSX, a `computed` or an `effect` and they re-format when the language changes.

limits.title: Native plural rules cover 41 locales
limits.text: From the next release, iOS and Android ship a CLDR plural table in the runtime: 41 locale tags from `ar` to `zh`, and English-style rules for anything else. On the web it is whatever `Intl.PluralRules` knows.

faq.q: Can I keep my i18next JSON files?
faq.a: For the common syntax, yes: `{{name}}`, `_one`/`_other` suffixes, `context`, nested keys, `$t()` and `ns:key` resolve the same way. Ordinal plurals, `{{- raw}}` and inline format options are the gaps.

The i18n row of the benchmark record: one process per operation and library, bun/JavaScriptCore, one run, i18next 26.5.11 configured with `escapeValue: false` so both libraries produce the same raw string. The date row is flagged: the two libraries pick different default date styles.
No. Pyreon writes translated text into text nodes, where markup is inert. If you put a translation into `innerHTML`, escape it yourself, or use `<Trans>` for real markup.

faq.q: What happens to a missing key?
faq.a: `t()` tries the current locale, then `fallbackLocale`, then `defaultValue`, and finally returns the key itself. `onMissingKey` lets you log it or return something else.

benchmarks.rival: vs i18next 26.5.11 · bun/JavaScriptCore, one process per operation and library
benchmarks.p: Every label calls `t()`, so the lookup cost is paid on every screen. i18next runs with `escapeValue: false`, its faster path, so both sides return the same raw string. The record lists no loss and no tie for i18n. The date row compares different default styles, so read it as indicative.
